# P27.6 (LAUNCH.6) — IA + navigation redesign + national landing + design system

## Summary

The full launch redesign of the public web surface (`web/`): a coherent national
information architecture, a grouped/uncluttered/keyboard-accessible navigation, a real
national landing page, a per-jurisdiction dossier index, real manifest-sourced citation
metadata on the canonical origin, and a cohesive design system applied site-wide — all
still zero-JS and WCAG 2.2 AA. Implements the operator-ratified **ADR-093** (national IA)
and lands the owed **§39–41 SIG-UI** spec fold-backs of ADR-090/ADR-093 (D-P27-SPEC-1).

Spec: `docs/tickets/P27.6__ia-redesign-landing.md`. Requirement ids: **SIG-UI-048**,
**SIG-UI-049** (minted here); honours SIG-UI-035/036/037/044, SIG-UI-010..015,
SIG-METRIC-009/010, SIG-ENG-003/039.

## What changed

- **Navigation + IA** (`web/src/layouts/BaseLayout.astro`): the flat 13-link bar → a
  grouped, keyboard-accessible nav (Explore · About the record · Reference), each group
  an ARIA-labelled `role="group"`. The hardcoded `/dossier/oklahoma-city/` link is
  replaced by the **dossier index** (`/dossier/`). No client JS.
- **Duplication reconciled** (ADR-093 §4): `/map/` is the one canonical map surface and
  `/network/` the one canonical network surface; the former `/reference-map/` and
  `/reference-graph/` demo pages are **deleted** and folded into `/visual-language/` (the
  reference page), where the map popup + graph edge list still demonstrate SIG-UI-008's
  "persistent across render paths".
- **National landing** (`web/src/pages/index.astro`): honest headline counts with
  **named denominators and no population total** (`assertCoverageMetrics` at build), the
  jurisdiction reach, product entry points, and the epistemic framing ("absence is not
  evidence of absence"). Reads `getCoverage()`/`getDossierIndex()`/`getFreshness()`.
- **Per-jurisdiction dossier index** (`web/src/pages/dossier/index.astro`): every
  publishable jurisdiction from the P27.4 dossier index, each linking to its dossier +
  print export.
- **Real metadata** (deliverable 4): `astro.config.mjs` `site =
  https://surveillancegraph.org` (canonical custom domain; DNS cut-over is P27.10). The
  belief-pinned permalink + `as_of`/ruleset come from the export **manifest**
  (`getSiteMetadata()` reads `<exportDir>/manifest.json` `reproducibility_inputs` in
  export mode; the fixtures constant only in fixtures mode), not the frozen `fixtures.ts`
  value. The shell's origin fallbacks (`citation.ts`, dossier/watch endpoints) and the
  evidence permalinks now resolve to the canonical origin — no `sig.example` in shipped
  output.
- **Design system** (`web/src/styles/epistemic.css`): neutral spacing/type tokens, the
  header + grouped nav, and the landing/index cards. Chrome uses only the neutral
  greyscale tokens — no `--sig-epi-*` token added, so saturated colour stays reserved for
  epistemic state (SIG-UI-006). React (`@astrojs/react`) was **not** adopted (optional in
  the contract); `.astro` + CSS keeps zero-JS guaranteed and adds no dependency.
- **Spec fold-back** (D-P27-SPEC-1): `SIG-UI-048` (§39.2) + `SIG-UI-049` (§39.9) minted in
  `spec_src/81_partVII_s39to41_ui.md`; spec regenerated via `BUILD.sh` (byte-identical);
  `check_spec_src.py` + `check_coverage_matrix.py` bumped 674→**676**; coverage rows added;
  DEFERRALS D-P27-SPEC-1 advanced (only the ADR-091 §40 island share remains, owed to P27.9).

## Design decisions

- **Fold, not remove-only, for the reference pages.** ADR-093 §4 allows "fold into the
  visual-language doc or are removed"; folding preserves the SIG-UI-008 cross-render-path
  demonstration and the SIG-UI-037 tabular/list equivalents in one reference page. Two
  fixture cross-links (`corrections`, `dossier`) were repointed to
  `/visual-language/#reference-map` to avoid dead links (a link value, not a data shape).
- **`DEFAULT_ORIGIN` = the canonical origin.** The library permalink default and the
  evidence-fixture permalinks now use `https://surveillancegraph.org`; two tests asserting
  the old placeholder were updated. Built page permalinks already used `Astro.site.origin`.
- **No new ADR.** ADR-093 already records this IA decision (Accepted 2026-09-22); this PR
  implements it and cites it (SIG-ENG-003 — extend/cite, do not duplicate).
- **Out of scope, untouched:** islands/client JS (P27.9), empty-state/large-table polish
  (P27.7), deploy (P27.8), data shapes (P27.4/P27.5).

## Verification

- `npm --prefix web run check` **green in BOTH modes**: fixtures (typecheck 0 errors, 187
  unit, build, licenses, 197 e2e incl. axe WCAG 2.2 AA) and `SIG_DATA_SOURCE=export`
  against a fixture-equivalent bundle (197 e2e). `site` resolves to
  `https://surveillancegraph.org` (no `sig.example`, no frozen `2026-08-20` in the shell).
- Zero-JS budget: `check:perf` (lhci) passes on the public pages incl. the new landing —
  script size 0, total ≤150 KB, a11y = 1.
- `make check` green; spec regenerated byte-identical; `check_spec_src.py` (676 ids) +
  `check_coverage_matrix.py` (676 rows) exit 0; `check-build-memory.sh` exit 0.
